data.name: Justinianus
data.gender_notes: Justinianus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Latin 'Iustitianus', meaning 'just rule'. Justinian I (482-565 AD) was a Byzantine Emperor known for his significant legal reforms. The name Justinianus carries the meaning “Just rule” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Justinianus usually hope their child will grow to embody just rule and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Justinianus belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Just rule.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Justinianus total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: Justinian I is best remembered for his ambitious legal reforms, known as the Codex Justinianus – a compilation of Roman laws and regulations under imperial authority. His rule represented a golden age for the Eastern Roman Empire, restoring the Empire's territories and prestige.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Justinianus' embodies the ancient Roman and Christian virtues of justice, fairness, and righteousness. Emperor Justinian I was a devout Christian who tightly linked his imperial rule with his Christian faith, ruling with divine wisdom and fairness. The name is a powerful reminder of our responsibility to uphold justice and morality in our lives and actions.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Justinianus: From the Latin 'Iustus' (just) and 'ianus' (god Janus, symbolizing doors or beginnings), signifying a ruler who embodies justice in his beginnings and throughout his reign.

biblical_reference.note: not a direct biblical reference, but rather a name influenced by Christian tradition

historical_references.reference: Justinian I was a Roman Emperor from 527 to 565 AD, known for his extensive building program that included the Hagia Sophia in Constantinople.
Justinian I's legal reforms, compiled in the Corpus Iuris Civilis, greatly influenced European and Western legal systems for centuries to come.

modern_usage.modern_context: Justinianus is a name of ancient Roman origin, best known as the ruler of the Byzantine Empire from 527 to 565 AD. His reign marked the second golden age of the Empire, during which significant legislative, cultural and architectural achievements took place. In modern context, Justinianus is a frequently referenced figure in academia, particularly in the study of history and law. His legal code, the 'Codex Justinianus' or 'Corpus Juris Civilis', is the foundation of Roman law and is still in use today. Justinianus is also a popular subject in historical fiction, with numerous books, films and television series exploring aspects of his life and rule. Visitors to museums can also encounter Justinianus in various exhibits and displays, showcasing his historical significance and legacy.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named David Justinianus in Athens, Greece credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Justinianus, which means "Just rule". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
